title: The Reliever WAR Illusion — role inflation vs acquired skill
built_from: Player-level deployment feature: retrosheet_game_appearances (now 2010-2024) bridged to MLBAM via chadwick_register (100% match), joined to trade_player_war_window + trade_player_xera_window. Pre = season t-1 with origin team, post = season t+1 with receiver.
question: When a team acquires a reliever and 'gets X WAR' from him, is that skill he brought, or the role (innings + leverage) the new team handed him?

headline_decomposition_relievers.interpretation: Post-trade reliever WAR change is ~23x more explained by role/volume change than by actual rate-stat (xERA) change. Adding skill on top of role adds essentially nothing (0.001).

confound_magnitudes.note: Innings-volume change is the dominant driver of WAR change.

skill_does_not_move_or_transfer.interpretation: Deployment change does NOT predict rate-stat (skill) change. The small bf<->xera link is reverse causation (teams give more innings to pitchers already throwing well), not the team improving anyone.

among_relievers_whose_xera_got_worse.interpretation: Holding skill DIRECTION constant (xERA worsened), relievers who got MORE innings held WAR near flat; those who got FEWER cratered. A 0.67-WAR swing driven purely by the role the team assigned.

verdict: ROBUST and ACTIONABLE, but partially-known (like the xERA/DIPS finding). A post-trade reliever WAR bump is mostly ROLE ACCOUNTING — the innings and leverage the new team chooses to give him — not skill it acquired or unlocked. Don't pay a premium for a reliever's projected post-trade WAR; the high-leverage innings that generate it are a role you control and could assign to anyone, while the underlying skill (xERA) you're actually buying barely moves.
honest_caveats: Mechanically, WAR rewards role (innings count; reliever WAR is leverage-weighted via gmLI), so 'role explains WAR' is partly tautological. That mechanical-ness IS the lesson: the WAR number should not be read as transferable skill.

Reliever xERA is a noisy skill proxy in the small post-trade samples (delta sd ~10), so 'skill explains <1%' partly reflects noisy skill measurement, not proven zero skill effect. The clean, robust claim is that ROLE DOMINATES.
Relievers specifically (reliever_frac_pre>0.5, n=452). Starters' WAR is also volume-driven but less leverage-sensitive.

Direction (reliever WAR is role/leverage dependent) is known to sabermetricians; the fresh contribution is the trade-context magnitude (18% role vs <1% skill) and the hold-skill-constant 0.67-WAR role swing.
pairs_with: change-of-scenery-myth — both are 'what looks like value/improvement is actually X' debunks. This one: post-trade reliever value is the role you assign, not skill you acquired.
potential_article: The Reliever WAR Illusion — candidate companion piece; honest framing required (robust + actionable, direction partially known).
